analysis: The supplied units are only CHANGELOG.md head text (lines 2126-2612), documentation/release notes. There is no executable code, config, workflow, or threat model change in these units. I examined them against the threat model for any claims indicating a changed security posture. Relevant items: (1) the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041) changelog entries such as the GLM prefix store defaulting on for the pinned GLM identity, the DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_DEBUG_CACHE_KEY_FILE persistent key path (stated as absent from release builds), larger SSD restore staging caps (7 GiB/15 s on >=48 GiB Macs), and the unchanged daily write cap and 30-minute TTL. These are described as not altering HMAC naming, AAD, or scope, but the underlying code is not in this batch; the next pass should verify that the DEBUG key-file path is compiled out of release builds and that the GLM default-on cache respects the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch (T-041, TB-007). (2) Release pipeline notes: staging lane (STAGING_ENABLED gated, Developer-ID dev-family signing), reusable workflow, a dispatch-only dev-branch lane with ad-hoc signed release, and a relaxed installer signature check for versions containing -dev. or -staging. (still bundle-id pinned; production keeps the Apple-team requirement). This touches T-034/T-013/TB-003 trust in provider binary identity and the install path; the actual install.sh and workflow diffs are not in this batch, so the reviewer should confirm the relaxation cannot be triggered for production-version strings and that prod remains tag-gated. (3) Performance and memory features (video decoding limits, cold-load queue release, shape warmup) are DoS-relevant (T-010, T-029) but only described. No concrete security regression is evidenced by changelog prose alone; flagged items rely on unseen source, so deeper review of those sources is warranted.
